lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Add a headline or summary that makes the target ML and AI systems role clear.
items.because: Readers currently have to infer the focus from the entries below.

items.says: Consider moving experience ahead of education for experienced roles.
items.because: The work and project evidence may be more persuasive up front.

items.says: Put the experience entries in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The internship ended in May 2025, after the role that ended in July 2024.

items.says: Show the dashboards’ scale, what changed, and what improved for users.
items.because: Ownership alone does not show the impact of the work.

items.says: Show the operational impact of the on-call responsibility.
items.because: It currently takes up space without showing what it achieved.

items.says: Make clear that 200 ms is the load-test limit, not the achieved latency.
items.because: Readers could confuse it with the reported 180 ms result.

items.says: Clarify how the automated checks shortened the release cycle.
items.because: The causal claim needs to feel well-supported.

items.says: Consider a stronger verb than “Maintained” for the CI work.
items.because: It may understate a significant contribution.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the migration, logging, onboarding, and on-call contributions.
items.because: The crowded bullet obscures the main result and your role.

items.says: Clarify what the final “which” clause refers to.
items.because: Its antecedent is unclear.

items.says: Measure the backlog impact if possible.
items.because: A measure would make the result stronger.

items.says: Avoid repeating the on-call responsibility from the dashboard bullet.
items.because: The on-call references overlap.

items.says: Explain what “branch” means to an outside reader.
items.because: The term may not make the triage system clear.

items.says: Make the connection between the triage system and backlog reduction easier to follow.
items.because: The operational result needs a clear link to the work.

items.says: Add a defensible baseline or further measurement context if available.
items.because: It could help establish the backlog result beyond the eight weeks after launch.

items.says: Explain how accuracy was measured and what the held-out cases represent.
items.because: Readers may not know how comparable or meaningful the evaluation is.

items.says: Make the result understandable beyond an ML audience.
items.because: The loss-masking detail may obscure it for broader engineering readers.

items.says: Explain the workload and measurement setup behind “single-request” inference with dynamic batching.
items.because: Those terms may seem at odds to readers.

items.says: Make the latency comparison basis unambiguous.
items.because: The inference context is not yet clear.

items.says: Rewrite the opening to make clear who or what produced the result.
items.because: The current construction obscures attribution.

items.says: Prioritize the contribution and result over the list of methodological details.
items.because: The details come before a relatively modest 5% change.

items.says: Clarify the latency measurement scope and your specific contribution.
items.because: Otherwise, it is hard to judge whether the implementation detail earns its space.

items.says: Show evidence that training became more stable or explain the one-trajectory tradeoff.
items.because: The bullet says what you did without showing why it mattered.

items.says: Use spelling consistent with the rest of the résumé.
items.because: “Stabilised” differs from the US spelling used elsewhere.

items.says: Show what the runbook helped reviewers do, if supported.
items.because: Adoption alone does not make its operational impact clear.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad “AI-first practices” bullet.
items.because: It does not say what changed or substantiate the claims about delivery and outcomes.

items.says: The 900 ms to 600 ms change is a 33% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: The incorrect arithmetic can undermine confidence in other metrics.

items.says: Clarify the tool-call latency measurement setup and workload.
items.because: The absolute numbers do not show how broadly the improvement applies.

items.says: A rise from 71% to 83% is a 12-point change, not a 12% relative improvement.
items.because: The two ways of expressing the improvement are different.

items.says: Describe the benchmark enough to interpret the task-completion result.
items.because: Its setup is not clear from the bullet.

items.says: Clarify whether this 71% baseline is unrelated to the internship’s 71% accuracy figure.
items.because: Readers could mistake the two figures for the same result.

items.says: Make your personal contribution to the upstreamed metrics clear.
items.because: “Upstreamed” may describe work shared with others.

items.says: Explain what was correlated and what the 0.89 value indicates.
items.because: Readers need that context to interpret the evaluator’s behavior.

items.says: Add the practical effect of the upstream fixes if available.
items.because: The bullet establishes debugging work but not its downstream effect.

items.says: Clarify how the three defects relate to stability, sourcing, and parameter handling.
items.because: The current phrasing is hard to parse.

items.says: Expand the skills section with relevant skills already demonstrated elsewhere, if accurate.
items.because: The short list makes CI, inference serving, and evaluation hard to find quickly.

items.says: Consider replacing Git with a more differentiating skill.
items.because: Git is a low-distinction item for many engineering roles.

items.says: Make skill entries more consistent in specificity.
items.because: The section mixes tools, methods, and broad capabilities.

items.says: Reconsider placing Kubernetes under “ML & Agents.”
items.because: The heading mixes infrastructure with methods and concepts.
